title: Quick-Ship SDK Beta Circuit Playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose and intent:
This is a working draft for a compact, production-minded quickstart and telemetry "circuit" for SDK beta adopters. The goal: get teams from zero to a validated sample integration in <=30 minutes, plus a purposely small set of telemetry signals that let us detect early regressions in latency, token cost, and prompt-quality.

High-level goals:
- 30-minute developer happy path: auth -> run sample request -> stream -> inspect telemetry -> toggle failover.
- Minimal cognitive load: single-file quickstart with clear knobs (api key, model, streaming).
- Early-warning telemetry: three signals (p95 latency, token burn delta, sample prompt accuracy drift).
- Circuit test harness: lightweight chaos injection for offline QA and a canary flow for production rollouts.

Audience and constraints:
- Audience: product engineers evaluating Redwood SDKs (js/python), solutions engineers doing demos, and early beta customers.
- Constraints: assume no infra changes for adopters; keep network assumptions to standard company proxies, allow offline stub mode for PoCs.

Beta Circuit components (compact):
1) Quickstart file (single script):
   - index.md + run.sh / run.ps1 + minimal code example in JS and Python.
   - explicit environment variables: REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_MODEL, REDWOOD_REGION.
   - expected output example so users can sanity-check.

2) Telemetry shim (opinionated):
   - Local debug logs (levelled): info, warn, error.
   - Telemetry emission: p95_latency_ms, token_count_total, sample_prompt_quality_ratio.
   - Exporters: console, simple JSON file, optional push to customer's telemetry sink (instructions).

3) Canary/circuit harness:
   - Local canary runner (node/python script) that runs 10 representative prompts and records the three signals.
   - Chaos knobs: random delay injection, truncated streaming, rate-limit responses.
   - Pass/fail criteria: p95 < 400ms, token burn within ±15% of baseline, prompt_quality_ratio >= 0.85.

4) Short README for SEs and support:
   - Troubleshooting checklist with quick commands (curl to runtime, inspect cache hits, fallback to smaller model).
   - Runbook for common beta issues (auth errors, regional misroute, high-cost spikes).

Quickstart UX sketch (30-min path):
- 0–3m: clone repo, set REDWOOD_API_KEY from invite email, set REDWOOD_MODEL=delta-mini (example).
- 3–8m: run "npm install" or "pip install -r requirements.txt"; run sample success path.
- 8–12m: observe streaming output, toggle streaming vs non-streaming mode.
- 12–18m: run local canary runner; compare JSON telemetry to expected baseline.
- 18–25m: flip one chaos knob (e.g., 200ms delay) to see circuit reaction; practice fallback (switch model or enable local stub).
- 25–30m: file first bug report using template (see linked artifacts).

Telemetry signal definitions (simple):
- p95_latency_ms: 95th percentile round-trip time measured at client-side (ms).
- token_count_total: tokens emitted per request (model-reported where available).
- sample_prompt_quality_ratio: fraction of golden prompts that produced acceptable outputs (binary pass/fail per sample).

Why these signals?
- p95 catches tail-latency which disrupts UX.
- token_count_total surfaces sudden billing regressions when model changes or prompt templates expand.
- sample_prompt_quality_ratio is a cheap, human-curated guard against quality regressions (used to gate rollouts).

Implementation notes (developer-facing):
- Provide JS and Python snippets that call Redwood SDK with a stable shape:
  - createClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, region: process.env.REDWOOD_REGION })
  - client.stream({ model: process.env.REDWOOD_MODEL, messages: [...] })
- Telemetry shim wraps the client request and measures start/end, token estimates (aka token_count_total), and runs golden prompt checks in a separate harness.
- Canary runner stores baseline JSON under /telemetry/baselines/beta-v1.json committed in the repo.

Failure scenarios to surface in docs:
- Auth misconfiguration: helpful error, link to support key reset.
- Region mismatch: explicit error message and fix steps (set REDWOOD_REGION).
- Latency regression: how to capture flamegraph and tracer link.
- Token explosion: sample diff tool to compare token_count_total vs baseline.

Support and escalation path (beta):
- First 10 min: quick triage doc for SEs (console logs, sample request id, canary run output).
- Tier 2: attach telemetry JSON, example inputs, and group p95/token deltas.
- Escalation: tag eng-serving-runtime on Jira DEVEXP-412 with artifact links.

Open questions / decisions (for this draft):
- Do we commit a small set of golden prompts, or dynamically fetch them from a central repo? (tradeoff: reproducibility vs maintenance).
- Should the sample_prompt_quality_ratio be automated with a lightweight heuristic (BLEU/ROUGE) or always human-curated?
- Can we keep the canary runner dependency-free (raw curl + jq) or rely on node/python for richer checks?

Next milestones (short):
- Prototype quickstart script and telemetry shim (E2E) — owner: Maya — target: 2026-03-20.
- Internal SE dry-run + notes — owner: Ethan — target: 2026-03-27.
- Beta bundle for 5 customers + feedback form — owner: Lena — target: 2026-04-10.

Checklist for commit (minimal):
- [ ] single-file quickstart (js + py variants)
- [ ] local canary runner and baseline JSON
- [ ] telemetry shim + example outputs
- [ ] readme troubleshooting + support runbook snippet
- [ ] PR with sample screenshots and expected outputs

Notes to self (raw/working):
- Keep code tiny — panic comes from too many knobs.
- Include explicit sample error messages in README for SEs.
- Remember to add a quick note about private deployments (VPC) — stubbed flow must still pass.

References and links:
- JIRA DEVEXP-412 (beta orchestration)
- GH PR 198 (sdk telemetry shim prototype)
- Slack thread #sdk-beta (customer invites + keys)

If you want to run this locally right now: clone the toy repo (link in GH PR), set REDWOOD_API_KEY to the test key in the invite, run "npm run quickstart" (or "python quickstart.py"). Expect a short JSON file under /telemetry/output.json with p95/token/quality fields.

End of draft.
